request: a dark doom fusion in Darbari, key of D, teental, 120 bpm

seed_riff.reasoning: The riff grounds Darbari's essence into half-time doom weight: a massive low Sa chord on sam sustained over 2 beats, punctuated by muted chugs, then stepping onto vadi Re and komal ga before dropping to samvadi Pa on the khali (beat 9), finished by a tight 16th-note turnaround (S-d-n-R) driving back into sam.

phrase_plan.climax_and_sam: Peaks on madhya Pa before plunging through the g-m-R-S cell onto sam Sa

seed_head.idea: Solemn Darbari mukhada pivoting on slow komal ga andolan before crashing through g-m-R-S onto sam Sa

rhythm_section.reasoning: Darbari doom arrangement: Anchor the tonic S low with crushing sustained power chords and deliberate palm-muted chugs. In Section 1 (Mukhada), establish the definitive doom groove: massive S hit on sam, ringing through the sitar's ornaments, chugging on beats 2-3, moving to R-g grind on beats 4-5 and resolving cleanly back to S for the turnaround into sam. Sections 3 and 6 replay this signature mukhada pattern identically via same_as: 1. Section 2 (Manjha) plunges deep, sustaining long roots under the sitar's mandra andolan and answering the sitar's rest at beats 12-16 with a slow crushing descending fill (P-m-R-S). Section 4 (Antara) follows the raga's ascent: the guitar climbs to madhya/taar register (+1) with sparse, ringing chord hits on m and P (half-note/whole-note rings) giving space to the sitar's taar saptak reach. Section 5 (Taan) drives relentlessly with continuous chugging on the home pedal S, building driving momentum with half-step grinds into sam. Section 7 (Outro) concludes with massive ringing low S chords punctuated by silence and decaying distortion.

parts.role: Mukhada groove: crushing doom weight on S, chugs anchoring the middle, and tight turnaround to sam
Manjha: deep sustained low pedal under sitar meends, answering its rest on beats 12-16 with a doom fill
Mukhada return: exact replay of the main mukhada groove
Antara: sparse, ringing chords climbing an octave (+1) on m and P to let the sitar dominate the high register
Taan: driving home pedal chugs locking underneath the chaugun cascade with 16th-note turnaround
Mukhada climax: full aggression return of the gat head
Outro: long decaying power chords punctuating the sitar's final phrases into drone silence
